## Overview

`dbparser` is an [rOpenSci](https://ropensci.org/) peer-reviewed R package
that parses and integrates major pharmacological databases into standardized,
analysis-ready R objects called `dvobject`s (drugverse objects).

Pharmacological databases use incompatible formats and structures, forcing
researchers to write custom parsing scripts — a process that consumes
60–80% of analysis time. `dbparser` eliminates this bottleneck with
unified parsing functions, chainable merge operations, and a consistent
output structure that enables reproducible, cross-database analyses.

With recent updates, `dbparser` has evolved into an **integration engine**,
allowing you to merge mechanistic data (DrugBank) with real-world phenotypic
data (OnSIDES) and drug-drug interaction risks (TWOSIDES).

## Installation

```r
# From CRAN (stable)
install.packages("dbparser")

# From GitHub (development)
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ropensci/dbparser")
```

## Supported Databases

| Parser | Source | Reads | Tables returned | Licence of the source data | Since |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `parseDrugBank()` | [DrugBank](https://go.drugbank.com/) | The full database XML, or the zip it comes in | `drugs`; with options also `salts`, `products`, `references`, `cett` | not stated | 2.0.0 |
| `parseOnSIDES()` | [OnSIDES](https://github.com/tatonetti-lab/onsides) | A folder with `product_label.csv`, `product_adverse_effect.csv`, `product_to_rxnorm.csv`, `vocab_meddra_adverse_effect.csv`, `vocab_rxnorm_ingredient.csv`, `vocab_rxnorm_product.csv`, `vocab_rxnorm_ingredient_to_product.csv`, optionally `high_confidence.csv` | One table per file: `product_label`, `product_adverse_effect`, `product_to_rxnorm`, `vocab_meddra_adverse_effect`, `vocab_rxnorm_ingredient`, `vocab_rxnorm_product`, `vocab_rxnorm_ingredient_to_product`, optionally `high_confidence` | CC-BY-4.0 | 2.2.1 |
| `parseTWOSIDES()` | [TWOSIDES](https://nsides.io/) | `TWOSIDES.csv.gz` | `drug_drug_interactions` | not stated | 2.2.1 |
| `parseHPO()` | [Human Phenotype Ontology](https://hpo.jax.org/), as distributed by [Harmonizome](https://maayanlab.cloud/Harmonizome/) | `gene_attribute_edges.txt`, plain or gzip-compressed | `associations`, `genes`, `phenotypes` | CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 | 2.3.0 |
| `parseHGNC()` | [HGNC](https://www.genenames.org/) | `hgnc_complete_set.txt`, optionally `withdrawn.txt` | `gene`, `gene_name`, `withdrawn` | CC0-1.0 | 2.3.0 |
| `parseHealthCanadaDPD()` | [Health Canada Drug Product Database](https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-product-database/what-data-extract-drug-product-database.html) | `allfiles.zip`, `allfiles_ap.zip`, `allfiles_ia.zip`, `allfiles_dr.zip` (or their unzipped folders) and `inactive.zip` | `drug_product`, `active_ingredients`, `companies`, `form`, `packaging`, `pharmaceutical_std`, `route`, `schedule`, `status`, `therapeutic_class`, `veterinary_species`, `biosimilars`, `inactive_products` | OGL-Canada-2.0 | 2.3.0 |
| `parseOpenFDA()` | [openFDA](https://open.fda.gov/) | `drug-drugsfda-0001-of-0001.json.zip`, `drug-ndc-0001-of-0001.json.zip` (or the unzipped JSON) | `drugsfda_application`, `drugsfda_product`, `drugsfda_active_ingredient`, `drugsfda_submission`, `drugsfda_submission_property_type`, `drugsfda_application_doc`, `drugsfda_openfda`, `ndc_product`, `ndc_active_ingredient`, `ndc_route`, `ndc_pharm_class`, `ndc_packaging`, `ndc_openfda` | CC0-1.0 | 2.3.0 |

Each source keeps its own licence; check its terms before use. "Not stated"
means the source's own pages give no licence for the data; every parsed object
records the source's licence, terms page and requested citation (see
`get_source_metadata()`).

The DrugBank XML is downloaded from [DrugBank](https://go.drugbank.com/releases/latest)
with a free [account](https://go.drugbank.com/public_users/sign_up); versions
5.1.0 through 5.1.12 have been tested. If you find errors with any DrugBank
version, please submit an [issue](https://github.com/ropensci/dbparser/issues).

**Tutorials:** [Getting started](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/getting_started.html),
and the worked examples on [DrugBank](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/dbparser.html),
[integrated pharmacovigilance](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/drugbank_nside.html)
and [HPO target phenotypes](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/hpo_target_phenotypes.html).

## Quick Start

### Parse a Single Database

```r
library(dbparser)

# Parse DrugBank
drugbank_db <- parseDrugBank("data/drugbank.xml")

# Parse OnSIDES
onsides_db <- parseOnSIDES("data/onsides/")

# Parse TWOSIDES
twosides_db <- parseTWOSIDES("data/TWOSIDES.csv.gz")
```

### Integration Pipeline

The power of `dbparser` lies in its ability to chain parsers and mergers
together. Here is how you can build a complete pharmacovigilance dataset:

```r
library(dbparser)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Parse the raw databases
drugbank_db <- parseDrugBank("data/drugbank.xml")
onsides_db  <- parseOnSIDES("data/onsides/")
twosides_db <- parseTWOSIDES("data/TWOSIDES.csv.gz")

# 2. Build the Integrated Knowledge Graph
#    DrugBank serves as the hub. Chain the merges.
final_db <- drugbank_db %>%
  merge_drugbank_onsides(onsides_db) %>%
  merge_drugbank_twosides(twosides_db)

# 3. Analyze Results
head(final_db$integrated_data$drug_drug_interactions)
```

For a detailed case study, see the
[Integrated Pharmacovigilance Vignette](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/drugbank_nside.html).

## The dvobject Structure

Every parser returns a `dvobject`: a named list of tibbles (DrugBank's are
nested in lists by section), with a `source_metadata` record of the source's
release, licence and file hashes. The tables and columns each parser returns
are listed in [dvobject structures by parser](https://docs.ropensci.org/dbparser/articles/dvobject_structures.html).

## Use dbparser from Claude

dbparser.mcp lets Claude Code and Claude Desktop parse and read your local
database files through dbparser, with each dataset's source, release and
licence in every answer.

## Commercial support and extensions

dbparser is free and open source, and it stays that way: every parser for an open database is part of this package.

It is maintained by [Interstellar](https://interstellar-egypt.com), which also offers:

- **dbparser Pro:** loads licensed sources (for example DrugBank, under your own licence) and your private data into PostgreSQL, matches products and ingredients across sources, with scheduled refresh, release-to-release comparison and validation reports.
- **Services:** data integration, custom sources, analysis apps and training for life-science teams.
- **DrugVerse Scope:** one sourced evidence page for any drug or target, built on dbparser.

Questions or early access: info@interstellar-egypt.com

| | dbparser (free, open source) | dbparser Pro |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| Parsers: DrugBank XML (from your own download), OnSIDES, TWOSIDES, HPO, HGNC, Health Canada DPD, openFDA (Drugs\@FDA, NDC) (more coming). Each source keeps its own licence. | ✓ | ✓ |
| dvobject format with source, release, licence and checksum metadata | ✓ | ✓ |
| Merge DrugBank with OnSIDES, TWOSIDES and HPO, and subset parsed DrugBank and OnSIDES datasets | ✓ | ✓ |
| Documentation, vignettes and examples | ✓ | ✓ |
| Community help on GitHub Discussions | ✓ | ✓ |
| Cross-source matching: products, ingredients and salt forms joined across DrugBank, Health Canada, FDA and other registers | | ✓ |
| Licensed sources (for example DrugBank, under your own licence) and your private data loaded into PostgreSQL, with a licence gate per deployment | | ✓ |
| Your private data joined to public sources | | ✓ |
